I1.quote: Hydrogen uptake capacity of the carbons was measured by gravimetric analysis with a Hiden XEMIS Intelligent Gravimetric Analyser using 99.9999% purity hydrogen additionally purified by a molecular sieve filter.

I2.location: main, p. 2, Table 1 (Elemental analysis of cellulose acetate-derived CA-hydrochar and activated carbons)

I3.quote: Sample CA-4700 stands out with excess uptake of 7.0 wt% (−196 °C and 20 bar), which is ~30% higher than any previously reported carbon

I4.quote: The apparent surface area (hereinafter referred to simply as surface area) rises from 2001 m2 g−1 for sample CA-4600 to a high of 3771 m2 g−1 for CA-4700 and then reduces to 2864 m2 g−1 for CA-4800.

I5.quote: Porous carbons have been extensively investigated for hydrogen storage but, to date, appear to have an upper limit to their storage capacity.

notes: Sorbents are KOH-activated carbons (CA-4600, CA-4700, CA-4800) from cellulose-acetate hydrochar, 76.1-81.4 wt% C (Table 1); commercial activated carbon AX21 was also measured in this work (SI Table 4, 'This work').
